newsitem.title: USA: House clears airport infrastructure funding bill.
newsitem.headline: House clears airport infrastructure funding bill.

text.p: The U.S. House of Representatives overwhelmingly approved a bill to authorize $29.5 billion for federal aviation programs over the next three years.

The Federal Aviation Authorization Act of 1996, cleared by a vote of 398-17, includes $7.039 billion in grants to the nation's airports to improve infrastructure, security and air traffic control systems.

Sponsored by Rep. Bud Shuster, R-Pa., chairman of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, the bill would authorize $2.28 billion in fiscal year 1997 for airport improvement grants, $2.347 in FY'98, and $4.412 billion in FY'99.
Among provisions of interest to the municipal bond market, the bill would authorize funds for completion of a sixth runway for Denver International Airport.
It also would drop a provision in an earlier version of the bill that would have helped clear the way for debt issuance by the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority.
